title: Seller Swarm Tactics — Ops Cheatsheet (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, tactical guide for SEs, sellers, and ops to "swarm" a live pilot when inference issues surface (latency, errors, cost spikes, or quality regressions). Designed to be used in the first 4 hours of an incident during pilot/POC so the field can stabilize customer experience and buy time for a deeper fix.

Context & when to use:
- Pilot is live and customer notices visible regressions (p95 latency > SLA, fluent chat hallucinations, or cost unexpectedly high).
- Use this when you need a coordinated cross-functional response from SE, Platform, and Product to avoid pilot churn.

High level flow (swarm lanes):
- 0–5 min (Seller triage): acknowledge customer, safe script, collect telemetry request ids and example prompts, reassure with SLA-aligned statement.
- 5–30 min (SE + Ops rapid triage): run quick checks (model variant, region, recent deploys, traffic spike), enable read-only fallback if available, quantize or route to cached path.
- 30 min–4 hrs (Engineering mitigation + comms): implement interim routing, set token/burst limits, run A/B to cheaper variant, schedule rollback or canary, daily sync until stable.

0–5 min Seller script (short, copyable):
- "Thanks — I see this is affecting X. We have a rapid response running now. Can you share a couple example prompts and approximate times? We'll keep you posted every 15 min."
- Attach: request ids, example outputs, account id, approximate traffic volume.

Quick checklist for SE/Ops (first pass):
- Confirm model id + variant (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
- Note recent deploys/rollouts (check Redwood Console rollouts tab).
- Pull p50/p95 latency, errors, token rate for last 10m/1h.
- Check KV cache hit rate + cache warmup status.
- Are requests being routed across regions? (region mismatch can add 50–200ms).
- Autoscaling events or GPU pool saturation?
- Any throttling or 429 spikes?
- If embeddings-heavy, check batch sizes and embedding queue depth.

Rapid remediation levers (ordered by speed/risk):
- Route to a more stable model variant (e.g., smaller-quantized fallback) — immediate and reversible.
- Enable prefix/KV cache response mode or warm caches for top prompts.
- Adjust batching window down to reduce latency (cost up, latency down).
- Apply rate limits per route to smooth spikes (temporary).
- Enable streaming to reduce perceived latency for UX.
- In Dedicated: add temporary burst capacity if contract allows.

One-line battlecard snippets for execs / champions:
- "Short-term: We can route to an equivalent quantized variant to meet p95 while engineering reduces model context waste. Medium-term: Redwood Optimize recommendations will lower unit cost without sacrificing p95."
- "If latency is user-visible, switching routing policy to nearest-region + smaller-quantized model reduces p95 by ~30–60% in typical setups."

Technical handoff template (SE -> Eng):
- Account: <acct-id>
- Time window (UTC): <start> -> <now>
- Symptoms: high p95 / 5xx spikes / hallucination examples
- Telemetry: request_ids [..], p50/p95 values, error logs (attach snapshot)
- Actions tried: routing change, fallback model, cache warmup
- Requested next step: roll back last rollout / increase pool / run perf trace on kernel selection

Suggested 6-slide quick deck for customer sync (10 min):
1) Current symptom + impact (examples)
2) What we saw in telemetry (short charts: p95, errors, token rate)
3) Rapid actions taken (timeline)
4) Short-term mitigation & expected outcome (30–60 min)
5) Medium-term root cause / next engineering steps (days)
6) Success metrics + who to contact / cadence

Objection scripts & responses (common):
- "We can’t accept lower quality": "We’ll A/B a quantized / cached variant to validate equivalence on your test prompts; revert immediately if mismatch."
- "This is unacceptable — we need on-prem stability": "Private deployment options + dedicated pools eliminate noisy neighbor variance; we’ll map a migration runbook."
- "Costs spiked": "We’ll apply per-route caps and a cheaper fallback; Redwood Optimize will run an immediate suggestion to cut token spend by ~20% for your workload."

KPIs to show in follow-up (must include before/after):
- p95 latency, p50 latency, token per request, error rate (5xx, 4xx), KV cache hit rate, cost per 1k requests, model switch impact on accuracy measured via eval prompt set.

Commands & places to look (internal):
- Redwood Console: Rollouts tab, Model catalog, Per-route traces.
- Observability: trace ids -> link to tracing UI (paste snapshots).
- Slack: #pilot-support, #se-incident-hotline
- GitHub: ops-scripts repository (quick routing playbooks).

Visual assets to include in slide pack:
- Side-by-side waveform of model latency p95 vs token rate
- Small A/B table showing sample prompts and outputs (golden vs fallback)
- Architecture diagram showing routing policy and fallbacks (simple)

Playbook dos / don’ts (field-tested):
- DO collect concrete failing prompts — that’s what product/ML needs to debug quality regressions.
- DO keep customer updates short and time-boxed.
- DON’T promise permanent fixes; commit to interim SLA-aligned mitigations.
- DON’T flip multiple knobs at once in production (one change at a time).

Open questions / TODOs (for follow-up doc):
- Can we add a canned API-level switch to force cached responses for a route? (owner: platform infra)
- Metric: define threshold rules that auto-trigger a seller alert (p95>500ms AND errors>2%).
- Create an SE playbook card for Accounting stakeholders (cost defenses).

Sample quick links to paste into customer email:
- "We're investigating; timeline: initial mitigation in 30–60m. Technical contact: Jordan Kim (SE) / #pilot-support. Tracing snapshot: <link>"

Notes to self (rough):
- Test with a real customer corpus to get better hit-rate expectations for KV cache.
- Work with Optimize to build an instant 'fallback recommendation' that returns 1–2 safer variants + estimated cost/delta.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-04 initial brainstorm notes
- 2026-01-10 added technical handoff template (Priya Shah)
- 2026-02-28 expanded remediation levers and added KPIs

End.
